home.headline: Selling into Germany? The requirements are easy to miss. We make sure you don't.
home.lede: Shipping B2C to Germany comes with a lot of bureaucracy. We help you make sense of it and take care of the details, so you can focus on sales!

obligations.heading: Accessible Online Shop
obligations.text:
Your shop, checkout and customer account have to be usable by people with disabilities, measured against {de|EN 301 549}, and you need a published accessibility statement. If your company has over 10 employees or generates over €2m turnover, this isn't optional, so it's worth getting right from the start.

Since January 2026 the German market surveillance authority has been running its own checks, not only responding to complaints.

obligations.heading: GPSR Product-Offer Information
obligations.law: General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988, Article 19 — applies since 13 December 2024
obligations.text:
Every online offer has to show the manufacturer's name, postal address and electronic address.

If the manufacturer is not established in the EU, you must also name the responsible person in the Union. If the manufacturer is EU-established, it is itself considered that responsible person, so no additional name is required.

obligations.heading: Registered Packaging
obligations.law: {de|Verpackungsgesetz} — {de|LUCID} registration, required before your first shipment
obligations.text:
Every box, filler and label you send into Germany has to be registered in the {de|LUCID} register and licensed with a dual system. Registration is required _before_ the first shipment.

Marketplaces are obliged to block sellers who have not done it.

findings.issue: Two icon-only controls do not communicate their purpose to assistive technology.

v5.faqIntro: The essentials about relevance, scope and what happens next.

faqs.question: I am already based in the EU. Is the audit relevant?
faqs.answer: Yes. What applies depends on your business, your products, and your role, and getting that scope right is exactly the work we do for you. Being EU-established changes some obligations, but it doesn't remove the German-market requirements relevant to your webshop.

faqs.question: What does the audit cover?
faqs.answer: The agreed scope can cover accessibility and BFSG, GPSR and product safety, packaging and LUCID, consumer-rights e-commerce information and relevant product-specific information. Applicability depends on your business and products.

faqs.question: Does the audit cover my entire product catalogue?
faqs.answer: The €890 audit covers the representative and agreed scope confirmed before work starts. Catalogue-wide, specialist-product or unusually complex reviews may require a separate scope.

faqs.question: Is this a certification or legal advice?
faqs.answer: No. ElbeBridge provides a technical and administrative review with practical guidance. The audit is not a certification and does not replace advice from a qualified legal professional.

faqs.question: What happens after the audit?
faqs.answer: You receive prioritized findings and remediation guidance. If you want help implementing changes or checking them again, that work is scoped and quoted separately.

comparison.heading: How the audit combines automation and review
comparison.intro: Different parts of the work need different methods. The audit uses each where it adds value.

rows.us: Tested with axe-core against WCAG 2.2 AA and {de|EN 301 549}, then checked by hand with a keyboard and a screen reader. This is where most real barriers show up.
rows.ai: Finds only what a machine can detect, and reports that as the whole picture.

rows.us: We search the German {de|LUCID} register under your legal entity and tell you the date we searched.
rows.ai: Cannot see the register at all.

rows.us: We check that GPSR details appear on the product pages where they're required, not just a category listing, and tell you what we found.
rows.ai: Reads the requirement. Does not open your product pages.

rows.us: A screenshot of the failing element on your own page, the clause it breaks, and the date — a document you can hand to a developer or an authority.
rows.ai: A list of suggestions with nothing behind them.

rows.us: We never tell you that you are compliant. We tell you what the requirement is and what we found. The report generator refuses to print the word.

sections.heading: 5. What we look at when we scan a website

blocks.text: When you ask us to audit a webshop, we review publicly accessible pages within the agreed scope and process the business information needed to produce the requested findings. We do not sign in, place orders, access authenticated areas or intentionally collect customer data. Our crawler identifies itself and respects robots.txt; further information is available on our [crawler transparency page](/scanner).

Two of our processors are reachable from the United States. GitHub, Inc. hosts this website and is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; it also offers Standard Contractual Clauses. Google Workspace is contracted through Google Ireland Limited, with the same frameworks in place for any onward transfer. We tell you this rather than claiming everything stays in Europe, because it does not.
Under the GDPR you have the right to:

items: access the personal data we hold about you (Article 15);
receive it in a portable format (Article 20);
object to processing based on legitimate interest (Article 21).

blocks.text: To exercise any of these, write to [hallo@elbebridge.com](mailto:hallo@elbebridge.com). You do not need to give a reason and it costs you nothing.

You can complain to a data protection supervisory authority. The competent authority for us is the {de|Hamburgische Beauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit} (Hamburg Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information).
If we change how we handle data, we update this page and the date at the top. We keep previous versions on file.

legal.title: Accessibility statement
legal.metaDescription: How accessible this website is, how we tested it, and how to tell us if something does not work for you.
legal.intro: We ask other companies about their accessibility statement, so here is ours. This statement covers the website at ElbeBridge.com and was last reviewed on 15 August 2026.

blocks.text: We believe this site conforms to {de|EN 301 549} and the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines 2.2 at level AA. Specifically:

items: every page works with the keyboard alone, and the focus indicator is always visible;
the site ships no JavaScript at all, so nothing depends on scripts loading;
text contrast exceeds the required ratio, and nothing is signalled by colour alone;
text can be resized to 200% without loss of content or horizontal scrolling;
the page structure uses real headings and landmarks, in order;
German terms inside English sentences carry their own language attribute, so a screen reader pronounces them correctly.

blocks.text: We assess this website regularly using a combination of technical and practical accessibility checks against the relevant requirements.
No single testing method can establish complete accessibility. We therefore keep this statement under review and welcome feedback about barriers we may have missed.
None currently recorded. If we become aware of a barrier we cannot fix immediately, we will list it here with a date by which we expect to fix it.

sections.heading: Tell us if something does not work

blocks.text: If you find a barrier on this site, email [hallo@elbebridge.com](mailto:hallo@elbebridge.com) and tell us what you were trying to do. We reply within one working days. If you need information from this site in a different format, ask and we will send it.

If you are not satisfied with our response, you can contact the German market surveillance authority for the accessibility of products and services ({de|Marktüberwachungsstelle der Länder für die Barrierefreiheit von Produkten und Dienstleistungen}).

legal.title: Crawler transparency
legal.metaDescription: Who operates ElbeBridgeComplianceBot, how to recognise it, its access boundaries and how to block it through robots.txt.
legal.intro: Our user agent points here so website operators can identify ElbeBridgeComplianceBot, understand its boundaries and contact us directly.

blocks.text: ElbeBridge GbR, Hamburg. We provide German Market Compliance Audits to e-commerce businesses. Write to [hallo@elbebridge.com](mailto:hallo@elbebridge.com) with any question about a request you have seen.
The crawler identifies itself, always, with a contactable address:
`Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; ElbeBridgeComplianceBot/1.0; +https://ElbeBridge.com/scanner)`
The identifying address links back to this transparency page and our contact details.
The crawler is limited to publicly accessible pages relevant to an agreed or requested review:

items: it does not access authenticated or customer-account areas;
it does not submit forms, add products to a basket or place orders.

blocks.text: If you believe an access fell outside these boundaries, contact us and we will investigate.
Access is kept proportionate to the requested review and designed to avoid unnecessary load on the website.
We read robots.txt on every request and honour it. To keep us out entirely, add these two lines:
`User-agent: ElbeBridgeComplianceBot`
`Disallow: /`
A disallowed site is recorded as skipped and nothing further is requested. If you would rather tell us directly, email us and we will remove the domain from the list.

We keep the information needed to deliver the requested audit and meet our business obligations. Audit findings are confidential and are not sold to third parties. We do not intentionally collect customer data. See our [privacy policy](/privacy) for details.
